source.author: Paventhan Vivekanandan
source.title: A Type-based Formal Specification for Cryptographic Protocols
source.journal: Journal of Internet Services and Information Security

read_scope: Selected web-extracted passages only: abstract/introduction; OTP specification and universe interpretation; section 4 description of CryptDB and homomorphic correctness; section 7 limitations and future work. Not a full-paper read.

primary_source_observations.claim: Higher inductive types encode encryption and correctness laws as paths and higher paths, including OTP and CryptDB examples.
The author discusses difficulties mapping nonbijective and probabilistic encryption to the path interpretation, and lists security guarantees via paths as future work.

our_comparison_not_a_source_claim: Using higher paths for cryptographic correctness is prior art. The present finite-table candidate instead concerns extension and quantitative edge-distance obstructions for parameterized stochastic cipher families. A difference in the question is not proof of novelty, practical cryptographic advantage, or necessity of infinity categories.
